info.title: edifact — read and validate UN/EDIFACT against the published directories
info.description: The `edifact` command line tool: ingest a UN/EDIFACT directory distribution into a pack, inspect what a pack holds, and validate or project an interchange against it. Install with `dotnet tool install --global Edifact.Cli`.

commands.name: ingest
commands.description:
Read a UNECE release directory into a compiled pack.
--out <directory>             Where packs are written. Default: as resolved below.
--syntax <directory>          Where the ISO 9735 definitions live.
--no-strict                   Write a pack even if something went unaccounted for.
--include-prose               Keep the directory's descriptive text. Writes to
<pack-id>-prose, which .gitignore keeps out of the repo.

commands.name: ingest-codes
commands.description:
Read the EANCOM Part III directory into the code set
additions one message needs.
--pack <pack-id>              Which release it is layered over. Required.
--message <TYPE:V:R:A>        Which message to gather paths for. Required.
--element <code>              A data element to cover. Repeatable. Default: the five
the committed ORDERS guide covers.
--for <path-to-part2>         Derive the element set from a Part II message folder's
own UnavailableCode gaps, instead of --element.
--packs <directory>           Where packs live.
--syntax <directory>          Where the ISO 9735 definitions live.
--out <file>                  Write the guide there rather than to standard output.
--id / --name / --edition     Override what the document calls itself.

commands.name: ingest-eancom
commands.description:
Read one EANCOM message's Part II guide and the Part III
underlay it needs, in one step: derive the element set,
write both documents, and write neither if either read
reports a gap it could still act on.
--pack <pack-id>              Which release both documents are layered over. Required.
--out-dir <directory>         Where both documents are written. Required.
--part3 <path>                The edition's part3 folder. Default: the part3 folder
beside the given part2 folder's edition.
--packs <directory>           Where packs live.
--syntax <directory>          Where the ISO 9735 definitions live.
--edition <text>              Override what both documents call the edition.

commands.name: ingest-guide
commands.description:
Read an EANCOM Part II message guide into an overlay.
--pack <pack-id>              Which release it is layered over. Required.
--packs <directory>           Where packs live.
--syntax <directory>          Where the ISO 9735 definitions live.
--over <path>                 A guide this one will sit above. Repeatable. Needed
where EANCOM restricts to codes the UN directory does
not publish, which the Part III guide adds.
--out <file>                  Write the guide there rather than to standard output.
--id / --name / --edition     Override what the document calls itself.

commands.name: inspect
commands.description:
Print a compiled pack's manifest.
--packs <directory>           Where packs live.

commands.name: project
commands.description:
Write a message type and everything it names.
--pack <pack-id>              Which release. Worked out from UNH for a file;
required for --message.
--packs <directory>           Where packs live.
--syntax <directory>          Where the ISO 9735 definitions live.
--guide <path>                An implementation guide to layer over the release.
Repeatable; the order is the precedence order.
--xml                         Write XML rather than JSON. Interchanges only: a
linked message type has no XML form.
--out <directory>             Write one file per message there rather than to
standard output. Required for an interchange holding
more than one message.

commands.name: validate
commands.description:
Read an interchange and report what is wrong with it.
--pack <pack-id>              Which release to validate against. Default: whichever
one UNH says the interchange was written against.
--packs <directory>           Where packs live.
--syntax <directory>          Where the ISO 9735 definitions live.
--guide <path>                An implementation guide to layer over the release.
Repeatable; the order is the precedence order.
--tree                        Print each message's structure as well.
--quiet                       Report only errors, not warnings.
--round-trip                  Also write the interchange back out and report whether
it is reproduced character for character.
--acknowledge <path>          Write the CONTRL this report deserves there.

options.description: Where packs are written. Default: as resolved below.

options.name: --no-strict
options.description: Write a pack even if something went unaccounted for.

options.name: --include-prose
options.description:
Keep the directory's descriptive text. Writes to
<pack-id>-prose, which .gitignore keeps out of the repo.
